subject: Immediate SLO mitigation request — FinBank latency spike after model v3.4 rollout
messages:
From: Gloria Tang <gloria.tang@finbank.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, platform@finbank.com
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency increase after v3.4 push — urgent

Hi Jonas and Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained latency increase starting ~06:45 PDT after your reported v3.4 rollout this morning. Tail p99 for our /generate route jumped from ~420ms to ~1.8s and median is up ~300ms. This is causing downstream timeouts in our transaction enrichment pipeline. Attached is a short CSV with sample response timings and a couple of screenshots from our monitoring.

We have an SLO of p99 < 800ms for this route (per the production SLA), and this is a clear miss. Can you confirm whether any runtime changes or kernel selection updates were part of the v3.4 model rollout for the hosted endpoint we're using (model id: redwood-text-3.4-large)?

We need an immediate mitigation plan and an estimate for a fix or rollback ETA. If a rollback is required, please advise on expected behavior during the rollback (warm-up, cold-cache effects, short-term latency). We've opened a support ticket (FB-9872) and can hop on a call if helpful.

Regards,
Gloria Tang
Platform Reliability Lead, FinBank
gloria.tang@finbank.com

Attachments:
- latency-report-20260528.csv (sample p50/p95/p99 times)
- slo-uptime-screenshots.png (Datadog graphs)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Gloria Tang <gloria.tang@finbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency increase after v3.4 push — urgent

Gloria — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. Sorry you're hitting this. We're treating this as a Sev-1 and have already looped in serving/infra.

Immediate plan (actions we are taking now):
- Rishi's team is reproducing the traffic profile against the canary to validate p99 changes.
- If a regression is confirmed, we will pin your customer route to the redwood-text-3.3-stable model (rollback) while we root cause. Pinning should restore your prior latency profile within the first 15–30 minutes but note there may be short-lived cold-cache tail effects for a few minutes.
- We're preparing an SLA exception / credit proposal in case unit costs or availability were impacted.

Two asks from your side to speed this up:
1) Confirm whether you witnessed any errors (5xx) correlated with the latency spike.
2) If you can share a short sample trace id or request id we can target logs faster.

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until resolved. If you're available, we'll queue a quick call at 08:55 PDT to align.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Gloria Tang <gloria.tang@finbank.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Sudden latency increase after v3.4 push — urgent

Jonas / team / Gloria — quick technical update from serving: we've reproduced an increased tail when running a production-like token distribution against the v3.4 binary. Initial hypothesis: a change in kernel selection for the attention block (optimized path in v3.4) increases single-request setup time for sequences with mixed-length prompts; throughput steady but p99 jumps.

Mitigation options and tradeoffs:
A) Roll back to redwood-text-3.3-stable for FinBank's route (recommended immediate mitigation). Estimated timeline: 15–45 minutes to fully converge; expect short p99 spikes during cache warm-up for ~5–10 minutes. No data migration required.

B) Apply a hotfix to switch kernel policy for your pool (non-disruptive config flip). Estimated timeline: 3–6 hours with a measured canary run. Lower risk of warm-cache variance but longer to ship.

C) Leave v3.4 in place and tune batching/kv-cache settings at the routing layer (experimental; may not meet SLO quickly).

Given this is an SLO miss, I recommend option A immediately and B as follow-up to reintroduce v3.4 with the kernel selection change disabled for your workload.

I'll standby to trigger the rollback if we have approval from Sales / the customer. I'll also capture a short postmortem notebook and perf artifacts.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Gloria Tang <gloria.tang@finbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency increase after v3.4 push — urgent

Gloria — thanks Rishi for the clear options. Gloria, we propose the following immediate course:

1) Trigger an immediate rollback (option A) to redwood-text-3.3-stable for your production route. This is intended strictly as a mitigation to restore your p99 SLO.
2) Run a 2-hour monitoring window after rollback; if metrics are stable we'll keep the pinned model while engineering completes the kernel policy hotfix (option B).
3) We will prepare a formal SLA exception package outlining credits and the operational timeline; I'll share a draft DocuSign for sign-off later today.

Please reply with YES to approve the rollback and indicate whether you want us to schedule the DocuSign for SLA credits to FinBank's legal team or route it to your procurement contact.

If we don't hear back within 30 minutes we'll call the platform emergency number you provided.

Thanks —
Jonas
